advances: An obstruction to deducing proper traces from a small scalar buffer, strict quotas and geometric normalization alone.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The singleton closed minors have mass $2<3$, and the two adjacent pairs have mass $4<6$. These are the only nonempty proper closed minors. Positivity of $\ell$ follows from $q>0$ and $2-q>0$. The identity $\ell(-1)\ell(0)\ell(1)=c^3q(2-q)=1$ proves the required normalization. The fiber centroid is $0$, so fact d90ba05577427854 gives $E_{[-1,1]}(0)=2$. The within-fiber variance is $\frac12\int_{-1}^1X^2\,dX=1/3$, giving the stated formula for $b$. Since $q(2-q)<\varepsilon^6/1000$, we have $c>10\varepsilon^{-2}$ and $b>\sqrt{10}/3>1$.

At $(0,0)$ a pure-base cap has minimum mass $4$. For a nonvertical cap normalize its continuous coefficient to $1$ after reflecting $X$ if needed. The middle fiber and the endpoint fiber with $az\ge0$ are full, because $b>1$. The remaining endpoint has threshold $|a|-b$ in its continuous coordinate. It contributes zero length precisely when $|a|-b\ge1$. At equality its closed trace is a supporting endpoint, and above equality it is empty. This gives every minimizing tilt and proves the raw depth $4$. At any mark, the pure-base cap minimum is at most $4$ over $z=0$ and at most $2$ over the two endpoints. Thus $4$ is the global maximum.

To count all maximizing marks, compute the projective energy at any $-1<y<1$. In the definition of fact d90ba05577427854, the image under $X-y\mapsto (X-y)/(1+a(X-y))$ has interval length
$$
\frac{1-y}{1+a(1-y)}+\frac{1+y}{1-a(1+y)}
=\frac{2}{1-2ay-a^2(1-y^2)}.
$$
The denominator is maximized at $a=-y/(1-y^2)$, where both admissibility factors are positive, giving $E_{[-1,1]}(y)=2(1-y^2)$. The physical shift at $(0,y)$ is therefore $b\sqrt{1-y^2}$. By the whole-fiber capture and atomic-gap lemma it reaches the atomic depth exactly when $b\sqrt{1-y^2}\ge1+|y|$, equivalent to the stated interval. The boundary marks at $y=\pm1$ have zero buffer and an outward continuous cap of zero length, and the two endpoint bases have atomic upper bound $2$.

If $\ell=1$, the physical shift at every mark is at most $\varepsilon/3\le1/3$ because $E\le2$. At each mark over $z=0$, select a continuous direction pointing toward its nearer own endpoint and use a sufficiently large base tilt to capture exactly one endpoint fiber. The own contribution has length at most $1+1/3$, so the raw maximum is at most $2+4/3<4$, using the atomic bound at the endpoint bases.
statement:
For every $0<\varepsilon\le1$ take the actual body $[-1,1]\times[-1,1]$, with integer base $z=-1,0,1$ and continuous coordinate $X$. All three fibers have volume two, the total mass is $M=6$, there are $k=2$ occupied parities, and the within-fiber variance is $\Sigma=1/3$. Put
$$
q=\varepsilon^6/2000,\qquad c=[q(2-q)]^{-1/3},\qquad
\ell(z)=c[1+(1-q)z].
$$
The affine multiplier is positive, its volume-weighted geometric mean is one, and every nonempty proper closed minor $T=P\cap\operatorname{conv}(T)$ has $V(T)/M<k(T)/k$, where $k(T)$ counts its occupied parities. Use the invariant buffer $f(z,X)=(\ell(z)E_{K_z}(X)/M)^{1/2}$ with the projective energy of fact d90ba05577427854, extended by zero to the fiber boundary. The buffered cap convention adds $\varepsilon f(z,X)\sqrt{u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma u}$ to the through-mark margin, including the unshifted pure-base caps.

The mark $(0,0)$ has buffered depth equal to the atomic depth and to the global raw buffered maximum, all equal to $4$. After normalizing the continuous coefficient to $1$ by scaling and reflection, every minimizing nonvertical cap there has margin $X+a z+b\ge0$ with $b=\varepsilon\sqrt c/3>1$ and $|a|\ge b+1$. None has a proper section in any fiber. At $|a|=b+1$ the excluded fiber has a single supporting point.

More precisely, the full maximizing set consists of $(0,y)$ with
$$
|y|\le\frac{b^2-1}{b^2+1}.
$$
At the same $\varepsilon$, the constant multiplier $\ell=1$ gives a smaller normalized maximum.
title: Small invariant buffers can bind the atomic cap under strict closed-minor quotas
